candidates.spoken_line: In Antarctica's freezing Dry Valleys, a five-story waterfall pours blood-red straight out of solid glacier ice.
candidates.opening_visual: Full-bleed NSF photograph of Blood Falls crimson plume on white Taylor Glacier ice
candidates.rationale: Explains both the iron-oxidation chemistry behind the red plume and the 2026 marine microbe discovery in the outflow mud.

candidates.spoken_line: At minus seventeen degrees Celsius, water shouldn't flow—yet a red waterfall pours continuously out of Taylor Glacier.
candidates.opening_visual: Aerial view of red brine flowing across frozen Taylor Glacier terminus
candidates.rationale: Shows how hypersaline brine lowers the freezing point above a hidden subglacial reservoir.

candidates.spoken_line: For more than a century, explorers stared at a crimson stain pouring out of solid Antarctic ice—and guessed the wrong cause.
candidates.opening_visual: Field scientist with tripod standing before Blood Falls ice wall
candidates.rationale: Reveals how iron brine replaced the red-algae hypothesis and what 2026 DNA/microscopy sampling uncovered.
